### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s).

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via os mcp connect (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via os mcp connect (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os cloud login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/cloud/login.ts), os login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts), os mcp connect (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via os login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/index.mdx`  _(via os cloud login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/cloud/login.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`  _(via os cloud login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/cloud/login.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx`  _(via os cloud login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/cloud/login.ts))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/build-with-claude-code.mdx`  _(via os mcp connect (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via os login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os cloud login (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/cloud/login.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d76adc72bb02ba328e250402b79931411aad631e` — the merge of head `bde1e1b1763b38ffbe93ac31eafb6485ff5ebd35` into base `d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d76adc72bb02ba328e250402b79931411aad631e && git checkout d76adc72bb02ba328e250402b79931411aad631e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae bde1e1b1763b38ffbe93ac31eafb6485ff5ebd35 && git checkout -B drift-repro d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae && git merge --no-ff bde1e1b1763b38ffbe93ac31eafb6485ff5ebd35

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d2fc055a17058416b91d3867c7527ebb225817ae` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ccccb5b40fb2d770bcc095ab9d0ae6999e22b2a`
Local-runs: probe — one `node` evaluation of the URL parser on sample addresses, to test the opener's stated claim about what a normalised address can hold; no check-run measures it. Nothing of the repo was built, run or re-run.
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/open-browser.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/auth-flows.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/connect.ts, packages/cli/test/sign-in-page-opens-http-only-without-a-shell.test.ts, packages/cli/test/cli-launches-without-a-shell.pin.test.ts + .changeset/cli-browser-launch-http-only-no-shell.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

No card. Governing word: the maintainer's 「按高危接,立即派」, whose content is: only an http or https address is opened, programs are launched without a shell, the same-class Windows case is folded in; no `packages/spec` change, no device-code protocol change. Read: that word, the PR body, the file list, the net diff `0e83fe03..6ccccb5b4`, and the head's check-runs. The changeset is read for ② only. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs at read time: 51 — 28 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 7 still running (Test Core 1/10 to 6/10, and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). Whether the two new test files sit in a finished shard was not established; this record does not stand in for the running legs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Sign-in address.** The opener is started only for an address the URL parser reads as `http:` or `https:`; any other address is printed, with one new line, and the flow goes on polling. Exit codes, `--no-browser` and `--json` are untouched. Right: it is the governing word's first limb, and both device flows (`os login`, `os cloud login`) now go through the one opener, the two private copies deleted.
- **Printed lines.** "Browser opened automatically…" keeps its text and is printed only when the opener was launched; one new line covers the not-opened case. Right; see N1 and N2.
- **`os mcp connect`, the launch.** `claude` starts from an argv array with `shell: false` on every platform: by name off Windows, as before; on Windows by the absolute path of the `.com` or `.exe` the first absolute `PATH` entry holds, the current directory and relative entries left out. Right: the second and third limbs.
- **`os mcp connect`, the new refusal.** On Windows a `claude` that resolves to a `.cmd` or `.bat` is not run: exit 1 with a new line. The exit value stays in the command's existing set; the installs that reach it are new. Right as a reading of the governing word; whether it is the contract wanted is the open question in ③, and it moves the declaration in ② (M1).
- **`missing` on Windows** answers the existing not-found line with exit 1. Right.
- **Exported symbols.** `resolveClientExecutable` and the exports of `open-browser.ts` are module-level only: the package's `exports` map publishes `.`, `./console` and `./hook-body`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports neither module. `mcpClientRunner.run` keeps its signature. No published surface moved. Right.
- **Prohibitions.** No flag added or removed; no `packages/spec` path in the diff; the device-authorization request, its fields and the poll loop are untouched. Both hold.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli` at `patch` is the right level, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author writes moves. The `Clause-②` value `no` is right: nothing is widened and nothing is newly published.

The sign-in half is not a narrowing. The device flow defines the verification address as a web page on the authorization server, so withholding the automatic open from anything else makes the protocol's own bound real, and the flow still completes from the printed address.

The Windows half is a narrowing, and it is not below the contract. The same invocation, on a Windows install whose `claude` is the batch-file shim an npm global install writes, went from registering the server and exiting 0 to exiting 1 with a line to run by hand. That install is the one the replaced code was written for, the published CLI reference says the command runs `claude mcp add` for you, and this repo's own changesets mark moves of that kind as breaking (a command that now refuses and exits 1 where it ran; a response that is now withheld where it was served). The PR body calls it "Windows narrowing" in prose and declares no arm.

M1 (must-fix) — as the tree stands (option A in ③), the changeset and the PR body owe `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a `!` summary, a **BREAKING** banner with the FROM → TO pair and the one-line fix (run the printed line, or install the native Windows build), and the ADR-0087 disposition marker. The level stays `patch`. If the ruling on ③ replaces A, M1 is re-judged on that head.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The open question, A or B — escalated to the maintainer, not ruled here** (a fix that settles a contract is his).

- **A, refuse and leave the printed line (the tree).** Keeps the governing word in full: nothing is launched and no shell is involved. Risks: it takes the one-command registration away from every Windows install whose `claude` is an npm shim, and owes M1; the remedy is a line the user runs in their own shell, so the user's shell reads that line, not this command; a `PATH` whose first hit is a shim is refused even when a later entry holds a runnable build; none of it is measured on a Windows host.
- **B, read the npm shim and run its target with node.** Also keeps the governing word, on three conditions: the target is taken only from a shim shape the code recognises, it resolves under the shim's own directory, and node is named by an absolute path and started from an argv array. Risks: a second accept-set, a reader of a file format the CLI does not own and that differs across npm versions and across other package managers' shims, so A's refusal stays for everything unrecognised; the text of a file on `PATH` then chooses the script node runs, a derived judgment that needs its own bound and pins; which node runs it (the one beside the shim, the one on `PATH`, or the CLI's own) changes the runtime the client gets; and it is wider than the shape the governing word names, on a path nobody has measured on Windows.
- Either way a refusal remains in the tree; the options differ in who reaches it.

**The four source-pin allowances.** Each cited site was read.

- `commands/doctor.ts` `probeTool`: holds. Three callers, each a constant line.
- `commands/init.ts` `PM install`: holds. The flag is a closed `options` list and the detector returns the same closed set.
- `utils/skills-catalog.ts` `npm pack` on Windows: holds. The version is held to a fixed character set before use, also when it comes from a profile file, and the directory is one the CLI created and quotes. It is the same batch-shim case as the open question, answered the other way; that is consistent only because every argument there is validated to a fixed set, and the governing word rules the shell out for `os mcp connect` regardless.
- `commands/dev.ts` `--filter PACKAGE`: does not meet the pin's own written bar (S4). The text is the invoking user's own argument, so no boundary is crossed, but it is neither written by the CLI nor validated to a fixed set.

**Tests under `packages/cli/test/`.** In keeping: that directory is where this package's command-level and `*.pin.test.ts` files already live, the existing `mcp-connect.test.ts` among them, and nothing under it ships (`files` is `dist`). The order's wording is the seat's to square.

**Not measured on a Windows host**, by the PR's own statement: the opener's argv and the client lookup are pinned against mocks only. That is a flag for the seat, not a fix the dev can make from here.

**SQL push-down.** No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.

A security item is with the owner seat.

### ④ Design judgment

Tried to break it; what held:

- **What reaches argv.** Both flows hand the parser's serialisation, never the raw string, as exactly one argv element; the behaviour test pins the argv per platform. It always begins `http://` or `https://`, so neither `open` nor `xdg-open` can read it as an option. On Windows the opener and its entry point are fixed tokens ahead of the address, and the opener is named by absolute path.
- **Coverage of launch sites.** Every `child_process` load under `packages/cli/src` was read. The only launches that carry text from outside the CLI are the two device flows and `os mcp connect`; all three are converted. The rest start `process.execPath` or a fixed program from an argv array, or are the four allowances above.
- **Windows lookup.** No current-directory search, no relative entry, and `.cmd`/`.bat` never reach the launch on any Node version, because the resolver answers them before the runner is called. The extension order is fixed rather than read from `PATHEXT`, which errs to the safe side.
- **The pin on today's tree.** No `promisify`, no inline `require` or `import` member call, and no launcher dependency exists under `packages/cli/src` or in the package's dependencies, so the pin's four allowances are the whole population today.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — `open-browser.ts` rests the Windows hand-off on a stated property of the normalised address that is not true of every component of it (the probe). Make it true in code: `browsableUrl` answers `undefined` for an address whose serialisation holds anything outside a fixed character set, and one such address is pinned as printed, not launched. Component-level detail is in the reviewer's private note.

S2 (should-fix) — the new refusal is pinned at the resolver only. Nothing pins what the command does with a `batch-shim` or a `missing` answer on Windows: exit 1, the printed line, and that the runner is not called. That is the derived judgment the changeset publishes; pin it at command level, beside the existing not-installed case.

S3 (should-fix) — the source pin sees the spellings its header lists and no others. It does not see: an exec binding used as a value (`promisify(exec)`, a local alias, a destructure from a namespace), a member call on an inline `require(…)` or `import(…)`, a launch whose program is itself a shell, or a `shell` option set outside an object literal in a file that loads `child_process`. And an allowance pins a count per file, not what the allowed line is built from: `probeTool` is an exported wrapper, so a new caller passing a built line adds no finding. Treat any non-call use of an exec binding as a finding, name the shell programs, and pin each allowed site's shape.

S4 (should-fix) — the pin's header forbids an allowance for a line carrying text the CLI neither wrote nor validated, and the `commands/dev.ts` allowance is such a line. Make the two agree: either state the third class in the rule (the invoking user's own argument) or hold PACKAGE to a fixed character set.

S5 (should-fix) — the published CLI reference (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, `os mcp connect` and `os login`) still lists the old exit conditions and says the browser is opened without the http(s) bound. It sits outside the order's surface, so it is the seat's follow-up, owed with or right after this change.

N1 (nit) — the changeset says "opened" is printed only when a browser was actually started; the tree prints it when the opener was launched, and a missing opener is swallowed afterwards. The PR body's wording is the accurate one.

N2 (nit) — a launch that throws answers `false`, and the caller then prints the "not an http or https address" line, which is the wrong reason for that case.

N3 (nit) — a `PATH` entry rooted without a drive letter counts as absolute in the lookup.

N4 (nit) — the refusal line names one remedy; the changeset names two (the native Windows build).

N5 (nit) — the lookup's file test on a `PATH` entry that is a link or an alias rather than a regular file is unmeasured.

N6 (nit) — the PR body counts the detector self-test as 10 and 9; the tree holds 11 and 10.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cec0b8c3e17be598c978094ef18e585e84b1b8fe`

### ④ Design judgment

Tried to break it; what held:

- **The address rule against the parser.** Probed with ports (default, empty, 0, out of range), upper case, a trailing dot, IDN and full-width hosts, percent-encoding in the host, numeric IPv4 forms, IPv6 literals with and without a port, a zone id, userinfo, backslashes, a missing slash after the scheme, dot segments, an empty query or fragment, surrounding blanks and an empty string. Every accepted spelling is registered and printed as a lower-case origin inside the set (an IDN host as its punycode form); every other is refused. Read in the code, and pinned by five cases: a control character is refused on the raw text, before the parser can drop it. An empty origin never reaches the rule: the command answers it first.
- **The opener's set against real sign-in addresses.** `?user_code=ABCD-EFGH`, further parameters, a port, a realm path, percent-encoding, a nested address in a parameter, a fragment route, and non-ASCII text (which the parser encodes) all open. Refused, and printed with the line: an address with a raw brace, pipe, caret, backslash or backtick in its query, a raw brace in its fragment, or a raw pipe or caret in its path. No device-flow address in ordinary use has that shape, and the flow completes either way.
